summary.overview: The TP4 Python course is designed to introduce students to the fundamentals of programming in Python, with a focus on manipulating dictionaries, lists, and defining functions. The course applies theoretical concepts to real-world scenarios, such as managing contacts, translating text, and simulating an online store. Through a series of exercises and examples, students will develop a comprehensive understanding of Python programming and its applications.

chapters.title: Introduction to Python Programming
chapters.summary: This chapter introduces the basics of Python programming, including data types, variables, and control structures. Students will learn how to write simple programs, manipulate lists and dictionaries, and define functions. The chapter also covers the application of Python programming to real-world scenarios, such as managing contacts and translating text. By the end of this chapter, students will have a solid foundation in Python programming and be able to apply their knowledge to solve problems. The chapter's focus on practical applications will help students understand the relevance and importance of Python programming in various fields.
takeaways: Ability to manipulate lists and dictionaries

chapters.title: Manipulating Dictionaries and Lists
chapters.summary: This chapter delves deeper into the manipulation of dictionaries and lists, covering topics such as accessing and modifying elements, using dictionary methods, and sorting lists. Students will learn how to use Python's built-in functions to perform common operations on dictionaries and lists, and how to write their own functions to solve specific problems. The chapter will also cover the application of dictionary and list manipulation to real-world scenarios, such as managing an online store's inventory and processing customer orders. By the end of this chapter, students will be able to efficiently manipulate dictionaries and lists to solve complex problems. The chapter's emphasis on practical applications will help students develop a deeper understanding of the concepts and their relevance to real-world scenarios.
takeaways: Ability to manipulate dictionaries and lists

chapters.title: Defining and Using Functions
chapters.summary: This chapter focuses on the definition and use of functions in Python programming. Students will learn how to define functions, pass arguments, and return values. The chapter will also cover the use of functions to solve specific problems, such as calculating the frequency of words in a text and translating text from one language to another. By the end of this chapter, students will be able to define and use functions to solve complex problems and apply their knowledge to real-world scenarios. The chapter's focus on practical applications will help students understand the importance of functions in Python programming and how they can be used to simplify complex tasks.
takeaways: Ability to pass arguments and return values

chapters.title: Application to Real-World Scenarios
chapters.summary: This chapter applies the concepts learned in the previous chapters to real-world scenarios, such as managing an online store's inventory, processing customer orders, and simulating a translation system. Students will learn how to use Python programming to solve complex problems and develop a deeper understanding of the concepts. The chapter will also cover the importance of testing and debugging code, and how to use Python's built-in tools to identify and fix errors. By the end of this chapter, students will be able to apply their knowledge of Python programming to solve complex problems and develop practical solutions. The chapter's emphasis on real-world applications will help students understand the relevance and importance of Python programming in various fields.
takeaways: Ability to apply Python programming to real-world scenarios
Understanding of testing and debugging code
Using Python's built-in tools to identify and fix errors

questions.question: What does print(contacts.keys()) display?
questions.explanation: print(contacts.keys()) displays a list of keys in the dictionary, which in this case are the contact names.

questions.question: What does print(contacts.values()) display?
questions.explanation: print(contacts.values()) displays a list of values in the dictionary, which in this case are the phone numbers.

questions.question: What instruction can be used to replace the phone number of Chloé with '0611223344'?
questions.explanation: The instruction contacts['Chloé'] = '0611223344' can be used to replace the phone number of Chloé with '0611223344'.

summary.overview: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the requirements and specifications for an e-commerce system, including functional, non-functional, technical, and business requirements. The system must provide a user-friendly interface, secure payment processing, and efficient order tracking and management. Additionally, the system must comply with various standards and regulations, such as GDPR and WCAG 2.1, and provide features like loyalty points, discounts, and customer feedback collection.

chapters.title: Functional Requirements
chapters.summary: The system must provide various functional requirements, including user registration, login, and password recovery, as well as features like search, shopping cart, and checkout. The system must also allow administrators to assign roles and permissions to users, and provide features like order tracking and notifications. Furthermore, the system must support multiple languages, currencies, and payment gateways, and provide a user-friendly interface for customers to manage their accounts and orders.

chapters.title: Non-Functional Requirements
chapters.summary: The system must meet various non-functional requirements, including performance, scalability, availability, and security. The system must be able to handle a large number of users and requests, and provide a fast and responsive user experience. Additionally, the system must ensure the security and integrity of customer data, and comply with relevant standards and regulations, such as GDPR and WCAG 2.1.

chapters.title: Technical Requirements
chapters.summary: The system must meet various technical requirements, including compatibility with different browsers, devices, and operating systems. The system must also provide a secure and efficient API for external services, and support features like multilingual support, responsive design, and accessibility. Furthermore, the system must be built using a modular and scalable architecture, and provide features like automated testing and deployment.
takeaways: Compatibility with different browsers and devices

chapters.title: Business Requirements
chapters.summary: The system must meet various business requirements, including features like loyalty points, discounts, and customer feedback collection. The system must also provide features like inventory management, supplier management, and tax calculation, and support multiple payment gateways and currencies. Furthermore, the system must provide a user-friendly interface for administrators to manage the system, and provide features like reporting and analytics.

Diagramme d’activités UML  permet  de  représenter  graphiquement  le  comportement  d'une  méthode   ou  le déroulement d'un  cas  d'utilisation ,  à  l'aide  de diagrammes  d'activités   (une variante  des diagrammes d'états - transitions ).  Une  activité  représente  une  exécution d'un mécanisme,  un   déroulement  d'étapes séquentielles.  Le passage  d'une activité vers  une  autre  est matérialisé par une transition . questions.question: What does print(contacts.values()) display?
questions.explanation: print(contacts.values()) displays a list of values in the contacts dictionary, which are the phone numbers of the contacts.

questions.question: What instruction can be used to replace the phone number of Chloé with '0611223344'?
questions.explanation: The instruction contacts['Chloé'] = '0611223344' can be used to replace the phone number of Chloé with '0611223344'.

questions.question: What does print(contacts.keys()) display?
questions.explanation: print(contacts.keys()) displays a list of keys in the contacts dictionary, which in this case are the names of the contacts.

questions.question: What does print(contacts.values()) display?
questions.explanation: print(contacts.values()) displays a list of values in the contacts dictionary, which in this case are the phone numbers of the contacts.
